subtype: Setting boundaries with a self-focused person [Response]
passage:
Monday: Eshaan spent the whole group-project meeting talking about his own start-up idea, then told the professor the survey was "mostly my design". Farhan's jaw clenched. He wanted to argue until Eshaan admitted the truth. He didn't.
Wednesday: Eshaan texted, "Bro, what did your parents say about your results? Tell me everything." Farhan wrote back, "All good," and nothing more. Then he emailed the professor the survey drafts with their dates, copying the group.
The next Monday: Eshaan began, "I'll present the survey part since I—" Farhan said calmly, "I'll present the survey. You take the market section. That's what we agreed." Eshaan sulked. Farhan didn't expect him to change. He went to the gym afterwards, feeling lighter.

qa.q: What did Eshaan tell the professor about the survey?
qa.a: He said it was "mostly my design".

qa.q: What did Farhan feel on Monday, and what did he want to do?
qa.a: He felt angry, his jaw clenched, and he wanted to argue until Eshaan admitted the truth.

qa.q: Which of Farhan's choices protected him best, and why?
qa.a: He sent the dated drafts, shared little personal information and calmly stated the agreed split, protecting his work without chasing Eshaan's agreement.

qa.q: How might Eshaan experience Farhan's calm limit?
qa.a: He seems unhappy about it, since he sulks, but he gets a clear message that Farhan won't give up his share.

grounding: Over a week, a student stays calm with a self-focused teammate, stops arguing for validation, shares less and states limits plainly.

subtype: Setting boundaries with a self-focused person [Response]
passage: Raghav, you asked how I handle Sunil uncle at family weddings. Let your Gautam mama tell you. When I was twenty-two, Sunil and I shared a room in Chennai. Every conversation came back to him: his job, his bike, how everyone else was jealous. If I disagreed, he sulked for days, and I'd end up apologising. One day I just stopped arguing. When he boasted, I'd say, "Good for you," and change the subject. When he asked about my salary, I said, "I'd rather keep that to myself." And when he took my scooter without asking, I said plainly, "Not without asking. That's my rule." He didn't change, beta. I stopped waiting for him to. Forty years on, we still meet at weddings, briefly, and I enjoy the biryani.

qa.q: What did Gautam say when Sunil asked about his salary?
qa.a: He said, "I'd rather keep that to myself."

qa.q: How might Gautam have felt back when he kept apologising to Sunil?
qa.a: He likely felt worn down and unheard, apologising even when Sunil was the one sulking.

qa.q: What turning point changed how Gautam handled Sunil?
qa.a: He stopped arguing for agreement, kept personal things private and stated plain rules, like asking before taking the scooter.

qa.q: How might Sunil have felt when Gautam stopped arguing?
qa.a: He may have felt puzzled or annoyed at losing a reaction, but he could no longer pull Gautam into long sulks.

grounding: An uncle recalls staying calm with a self-focused roommate, sharing less, stating plain limits and not expecting him to change.
